question.leadin: Give the following about the Adams family.
question.text: John Adams was married to this early feminist, who advised him to "remember the ladies" in one of their numerous correspondences.
question.clue: This person wrote another letter asking to "remember the ladies and be more generous and favorable to them than your ancestors."

swap.text: This man was the first to sign the Declaration of Independence; according to legend, he wanted King George to be able to see it without his reading glasses on.
swap.clue: This first governor of an independent Massachusetts was closely aligned with Samuel Adams, and neither of them were pardoned by Thomas Gage following the Boston Tea Party.

question.text: The snake on the "Join, or Die" cartoon was adopted by this person as the nameplate of the newspaper Massachusetts Spy. Joseph Warren told this person to make a journey to alert of the upcoming Battles of Lexington and Concord.
question.clue: This man, who notably depicted the Boston Massacre, was later joined by William Dawes and Samuel Prescott in one mission.

swap.leadin: This work notes that "there is something very absurd in supposing a continent to be perpetually governed by an island."
swap.text: Name this 1776 pamphlet that strongly urges American independence, arguing that "the blood of the slain, the weeping voice of nature cries, 'tis time to part.'"
swap.clue: Another chapter of this work claims that a certain monarch did little but "make war and give away places".

question.leadin: General Howe occupied Philadelphia after this battle and forced Washington's army to winter at Valley Forge.
question.text: Name this British victory and largest battle of the Revolutionary War. It took place along a namesake creek which is a branch of the Christina River.
question.clue: During this battle, troops under Charles Cornwallis crossed Trimble's and Jeffries Ford to flank the American forces, who were engaged with a decoy force of Hessians under Wilhelm von Knyphausen at Chadds Ford.

swap.text: Along with John Sullivan, this general was in charge of troops at the Battle of Long Island. This general is said to have ordered "Do not fire until you see the whites of their eyes" to his men at the battle of Bunker Hill.
swap.clue: He was second-in-command to Artemas Ward in the Army of Observation, and along with Ward, Philip Schuyler and Charles Lee, was one of four major generals appointed by the Continental Congress in 1775.

question.text: This colonial governor of Massachusetts evacuated soldiers to Castle Island after the massacre. Colonists published letters written by this governor that allegedly showed his intent to deprive colonists of their rights.
question.clue: For actually leaking this politician's letters, Benjamin Franklin was removed from his office as Postmaster General, although the public fixated on this administrator's suggestion to abridge "English liberties."

swap.text: This American privateer fought in the American Revolution and famously said "I have not begun to fight!" aboard his command, the Bonhomme Richard.
swap.clue: This naval commander raided English coastal towns during the American Revolution, and defeated the British sloop HMS Drake in 1778.

question.text: The first suspended the New York Assembly, while the second, also called the Revenue Act, laid new import taxes on glass, lead, tea, paints, and paper. They differed from the Stamp Act in requiring the customs duty to be paid at American ports. For 15 points-the Boston Tea Party and the Boston Massacre were results of what acts passed by Parliament in 1767?
question.clue: The "Massachusetts Circular" letter was written by Samuel Adams in response to this program, and these acts led to the seizure of a sloop owned by John Hancock, the Liberty.

swap.leadin: Name these battles featuring George Washington.
swap.text: This battle of late June, 1778 saw Washington attack the troops of Sir Henry Clinton near modern-day Freehold, New Jersey. It's more famous for the actions of Molly Pitcher.
swap.clue: This battle ended the Philadelphia campaign, as Henry Clinton was commanded to evacuate to New York.

question.text: Hamilton wrote 51 of this series of 85 essays supporting the ratification of the United States Constitution, alongside John Jay and James Madison. The trio used the pseudonym "Publius" to write these essays.
question.clue: A group of men with "neither FORCE nor WILL" is the subject of its seventy-eighth part.

swap.leadin: After Arthur St. Clair's defeat at the Battle of Wabash, George Washington appointed this man as the Commanding General of the United States Army.
swap.text: Name this general, nicknamed "Mad," who fought against the Northwestern Confederacy. The second-most populous city in Indiana was built under this general's direction, and is named after him.
swap.clue: Following that victory against Blue Jacket, this man negotiated the Treaty of Greenville.

question.text: In Melville's Israel Potter, Potter tries to rescue this man from prison. This man led an operation that allowed for Henry Knox's noble train of artillery while he was leading a group who eventually replaced him with Seth Warner.
question.clue: This man was held prisoner by the British after unsuccessfully attempting to take Montreal under General Philip Schuyler.

swap.leadin: Its namesake wrote a letter to Horatio Gates stating that, "Heaven has been determined to save your country, or a weak general and bad counselors would have ruined it."
swap.text: Name this attempt to remove George Washington from his command of the Continental Army.
swap.clue: Another member of this group defeated Arthur St. Clair in a Pennsylvania gubernatorial election and John Cadwalader shot this group's namesake in the mouth in a duel.

question.text: This notorious British soldier known as the "Butcher" reportedly reveled in abuse of prisoners at Charleston. His men were accused of massacring Americans at the Battle of Waxhaws.
question.clue: Three lines by the Broad River were employed by Daniel Morgan to defeat this commander of the British Legion.

swap.leadin: This battle was fought immediately after the victory over drunken Hessians at Trenton.
swap.text: Name this New Jersey battle, a Revolutionary War victory that saw American troops spill across Quaker Bridge.
swap.clue: At a critical point in this engagement, John Cadwalader arrived with militiamen to support the fleeing forces of Hugh Mercer, who the British mistook for George Washington.

question.leadin: This woman's second husband, Joseph Ashburn, was taken captive by the British, and she went on to marry John Claypoole.
question.text: Identify this woman who was supposedly visited by George Washington in 1776 to create a flag for the new nation.
question.clue: The first flag of the United States was legendarily created by this seamstress.

swap.text: This Barnstable patriot attacked the Writs of Assistance as Advocate-General, but is better remembered for allegedly saying that taxation without representation is tyranny.
swap.clue: This man went on to resign his own place on the vice admiralty court in order to collaborate with Oxenbridge Thacher on a case involving Charles Paxson, who was issuing Writs of Assistance.

question.text: This Continental general was widely criticized for surrendering seven thousand men at Charleston. Washington sent this man to accept the British surrender after Cornwallis designated Charles O'Hara.
question.clue: Though this general commanded the right flank, the Hudson River separated his normal forces from the fighting during the Battle of Saratoga.

swap.leadin: Their notable leaders included Seth Warner and John Stark. FTPE.
swap.text: Identify this military force that was founded to oppose the attempts of outside New Yorkers to lay claim to New Hampshire Grants.
swap.clue: Fort Crown Point was taken by this militia in the leadup to the capture of Fort Ticonderoga.
